title: Jerusalem restored; fasts become feasts; the nations seek the LORD (Zech 8)
speaker: The LORD of Armies through Zechariah
description: The LORD will return to Zion; old and young will fill Jerusalem's streets; he will gather his people from east and west; the seed will prosper; the fasts of the 4th, 5th, 7th and 10th months will become feasts; many peoples will come to seek the LORD in Jerusalem, and ten men from the nations will grasp a Jew's robe saying "God is with you".
in_text_interpretation: The text gives no time-frame beyond "in those days" (8:23).

interpretations.label: Fulfilled ultimately in the Messiah's future (millennial) reign in Jerusalem
proponents: C. L. Feinberg (as cited by Barker, via Guzik)
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: nations streaming to Jerusalem and the gathering of Israel exceed anything in the Persian period. Objection: the passage also addresses the builders of 518 directly (8:9–13).

referents.symbol: Ten men grasping a Jew's robe
referents.referent: The nations drawn to Israel in the Messiah's reign

interpretations.label: The nations come to God through the Jew Jesus (Christian, spiritual fulfilment)
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: "a Jew" read of Christ, through whom the nations approach God. Objection: the plural "Jews" context (8:13, 23) speaks of the people.
